items.detail: The **S&P 500** fell 0.23% to 7,323.63 Wednesday, a fifth straight loss that took it below its 200-day average, while the Nasdaq rose 0.42% to 24,429.89.
items.why: Hawkish Fed minutes and Nvidia's fading post-earnings rally kept pressure on the broader market.

items.detail: Minutes from the October Fed meeting showed nearly every official leaning toward **more rate hikes**, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%.
items.why: Officials saw a growing risk that they will have to tighten further to bring inflation under control.

items.detail: Anthropic priced its IPO at **$83 a share**, above its target range, raising about $81 billion at a roughly $1.5 trillion valuation before trading starts today on Nasdaq.
items.why: Orders came in about seven times the shares on offer, a sign that appetite for AI stocks is still strong.

items.detail: MSCI's Asia-Pacific index outside Japan slipped 0.3% Thursday and is on track for a weekly drop of **more than 4%**, with Taiwan down about 1%.
items.why: A stronger dollar and higher yields after the Fed minutes outweighed the lift from Anthropic's IPO pricing.

items.detail: The **Sensex** rose about 300 points to 82,339 early Thursday after Wednesday's 500-point drop, as auto stocks jumped 3.3%.
items.why: Autos and banks bounced back from the midweek slump, while IT stocks stayed weak on worries about more Fed hikes.

items.detail: US small caps beat the large caps Wednesday: the **S&P SmallCap 600** rose 0.68% and the Russell 2000 gained 0.46%, while the S&P 500 fell.
items.why: Small caps recovered part of Tuesday's 1.5% slide as selling hit megacaps and the Dow instead.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** fell 3.84% to $62,386.56 Wednesday, slipping back toward Sunday's low near $62,000.
items.why: The Fed minutes made a December hike look nearly certain and pushed yields above 5%, which hurt risk assets.

items.detail: **Ether** dropped 3.80% to $1,753.33, extending its slide further below $1,800.
items.why: It followed bitcoin lower as the hawkish Fed minutes and a strong dollar kept buyers away.

items.detail: **Solana** lost its recent edge, falling 2.88% to $72.94, though it is still holding above last weekend's four-month low.
items.why: The selloff after the Fed minutes hit the whole crypto market, which ended Solana's run as the lone gainer.

items.detail: **Gold** plunged 3.24% to $3,724.71 Wednesday, adding to its break below $3,800 and setting a new low since September 2025.
items.why: The hawkish Fed minutes lifted the dollar and Treasury yields, which makes gold less attractive.

crossCuttingTheme: Fed minutes showing nearly every official leaning toward more hikes lifted the dollar and yields, sinking gold more than 3% and dragging down crypto and Asian stocks, while Anthropic's record IPO pricing was tech's only support.
